profile.name: Dipesh Pansuriya
profile.tagline: I build systems that move data — reliably, at volume, without drama.

hero.headline: I build systems that move data.
hero.subline: Software engineer working on the unglamorous parts — correctness, throughput and the quiet machinery that keeps a product boring in production.

chapters.label: Start
chapters.title: Hello — I'm Dipesh.
chapters.body: A software engineer who likes the parts of the job nobody puts on a slide: schema design, retry semantics, the test that catches the regression three months later.
bullets: Thirteen years across product teams and platform work
Happiest when a system gets quieter as it grows
Based in Mumbai, working with teams across time zones

chapters.label: Craft
chapters.title: How I build.
chapters.body: Boundaries first, frameworks second. The rules of a system should be readable without a database, a queue or a container in the room — everything else is plumbing you can replace.
bullets: Domain logic stays pure and independently testable
Every failure leaves a trace, a metric and a replay path
Upgrade paths are designed, not discovered

chapters.label: Principles
chapters.title: What I optimise for.
chapters.body: Three rules that have survived every rewrite, every stack change and every deadline.
bullets: Boring in production beats clever in review
A system you can explain in one sentence is a system you can debug at 3am
Motion and interface should carry meaning, never decoration

chapters.label: Now
chapters.title: What I'm exploring.
chapters.body: Interface craft, developer experience, and the local-first tools that make a single machine feel like a small, well-run platform.
bullets: Interaction design for dense, technical products
Tooling that shortens the distance between idea and feedback
Anything that makes correctness cheaper than debugging

chapters.label: Contact
chapters.title: Say hello.
chapters.body: Open to conversations about platform work, integration architecture and interface craft. Email is the fastest route — I read everything.
bullets: Happy to talk architecture without a pitch deck

principles.title: Boundaries before frameworks
principles.body: Domain logic stays pure. Frameworks live at the edge, so the rules stay testable and the upgrade path stays cheap.

principles.title: Observability is a feature
principles.body: If a message can fail, it needs a trace, a metric and a replay path. Silent failure is the only unacceptable outcome.

principles.title: Motion with intent
principles.body: Animation should explain hierarchy and state. If it does not carry meaning, it is noise — and it costs frames.

contact.heading: Have a system that needs to hold up?
contact.body: I am open to conversations about platform work, integration architecture and frontend craft.
